newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end down 1/8 to 3/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end down 1/8 to 3/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended down 1/8 to 3/8 of a point as big new issues by the New York City Municipal Assistance Corp and the Chicago School Reform Board diverted market focus from the secondary.

"I would say munis are down about 3/8 of a point after putting in a very lackluster performance today," a trader said. "MACs were priced today and the Chicago Board of Ed deal was done today. I think that just dominated the customers, we saw nothing in the secondary."

JP Morgan Securities Inc repriced $528 million New York City Municipal Assistance Corp bonds, lowering yields in several maturities. The top yield in 2005 was lowered to 5.15 percent from 5.175 percent.
Goldman Sachs & Co repriced a $500 million Chicago School Reform Board of Trustees bond deal, cutting yields in several maturities, but raising the top yield in 2027 to 6.05 from 6.03 percent.

Also Wednesday, Morgan Stanley & Co repriced $129 million Michigan Hospital Finance Authority bonds, lowering yields in several maturities. The top yield remained in 2028 remained unchanged at 6.05 percent.
A municipal analyst called pricing on Wednesday's deals "firm."
"I think the issuer did well and the buyers did well on that stuff," he said, citing the MAC and Chicago deals.
Meanwhile, players were still wondering if a $932 million Port Authority of New York and New Jersey airport deal via Lehman Brothers would arrive this week or next.
"What we heard was (a) 20 percent chance tomorrow, and (an) 80 percent chance Friday," a trader outside the firm said.
An official at Lehman Brothers said while a decision has yet to be made, the firm would prefer to get the deal done this week.

Back in the secondary market, an analyst judged muni cash down 1/8 point overall. High-grade issues were down slightly, with weakness most apparent on the shorter and longer ends of the curve. Dollar bonds ended down 1/8 point-plus. Activity was light.
In debt futures, the June municipal contract closed down 11/32 at 112-20/32. The June T-bond contract closed down 13/32 at 107-23/32. The MOB spread was 157 ticks.
In the government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 16/32 at 94-10/32 to yield 7.08 percent.
Municipal bond sales for Thursday, April 24 are expected to total $460 million in 19 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $319 million in five sales, with a $154 million Virginia Public Building Authority deal through Craigie Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 14 sales totaling $141 million are on the schedule. A $44 million Milwaukee, Wis., deal at 1100 EDT is the largest.
